subject: Business
title: Crossing the Chasm
description: A micro-lesson that makes Crossing the Chasm usable.

hook.text: Your early adopters love you. Mainstream customers don't care. There's a chasm between them.

buildup.text: Geoffrey Moore showed that tech adoption has a dangerous gap between early and mainstream users.

discovery.text: Early adopters tolerate bugs and half-built products. The majority demands polish and social proof.

twist.text: Many startups stall at a few thousand users. They saturated early adopters but can't cross over.

climax.text: The strategy: pick one mainstream niche, dominate it completely, then expand outward.

punchline.text: Don't try to please everyone. Win one beachhead first.

quiz.question: What is the 'chasm' in technology adoption?
options: The gap between early adopters and the mainstream majority
The gap between idea and launch

details.summary: Geoffrey Moore's Crossing the Chasm identifies a dangerous gap between early adopters who love new technology and the pragmatic mainstream majority who need proven solutions. Many startups die in this chasm because the strategies that win early adopters fail with mainstream customers.
details.whyItMatters: Startups often mistake early adopter enthusiasm for mainstream demand. The chasm is where promising companies stall because they cannot translate visionary appeal into practical value for risk-averse mainstream buyers who need different messaging
takeaways: A dangerous gap separates enthusiastic early adopters from cautious mainstream buyers
Strategies that win early adopters fail with the pragmatic mainstream majority
Focus on dominating one niche beachhead before expanding to broader markets

faq.question: How does a startup cross the chasm successfully?
faq.answer: Choose a single niche market segment as your beachhead. Become the dominant solution in that niche. Use references and case studies from the niche as proof for adjacent segments. Pragmatic buyers need to see peers succeeding before they adopt. Expand concentrically from your beachhead.

faq.question: What are the signs that a startup is stuck in the chasm?
faq.answer: Initial sales were strong but growth has plateaued. Early customers love the product but new sales cycles are getting longer. Mainstream prospects ask for references from companies like theirs. The team feels they are pushing harder for diminishing returns.
